items.title: Roomba 115, 415, 515 e 575, in promo i robot multifunzione che arrivano dove gli altri si fermano
items.summary: Più bassi e raccolti del Roomba 505, aspirano e lavano sotto letti e divani. Si parte dal 115 con navigazione laser e si arriva al 575, che riconosce gli ostacoli e lava i panni a 75 °C ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Aspirano, lavano i pavimenti e soprattutto entrano dove un robot più ingombrante resta fuori : sotto il letto, sotto il divano, tra le gambe di sedie e tavoli. Roomba 115, 415, 515 e 575 sono i Roomba multifunzione più piccoli di sempre , fino al 21% più sottili del Roomba Plus 505.

Nessuno dei quattro rinuncia a qualcosa per stare in poco spazio , e salendo di modello si aggiungono la base che lava i panni, l'acqua calda e la visione artificiale.

Il vantaggio della taglia si conta in centimetri. Se il Roomba Plus 505 è alto 10,6 cm, il 415 e il 575 si fermano a 8,35 cm e il 115 a 9,2 cm. Sotto un divano o una rete del letto bastano quei due centimetri per far passare il robot proprio dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata , perché con la scopa non ci arriva nessuno. Anche la pianta si restringe: il 415 misura 29,8 per 30,3 cm, contro i 35,7 per 35,1 cm del 505, e si infila più facilmente tra le gambe di sedie e tavoli.

Tutti e quattro sono Combo, cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa sessione , e tutti si orientano con ClearView LiDAR. È un sensore laser che mappa la casa in meno di dieci minuti , funziona anche con poca luce e fa pulire il robot per file ordinate, stanza dopo stanza, invece che a caso. Quando incontra un tappeto, il robot lo riconosce e non lo bagna.

Le mappe si gestiscono dall'app Roomba Home , dove si programmano le pulizie, si scelgono le stanze e si regola l'intensità su quattro livelli di aspirazione. Il robot risponde anche ai comandi vocali di Alexa, Siri e Google Assistant . Le spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, infine, non si avvolgono di capelli e peli degli animali.

Il Roomba 115 Combo è la porta d'ingresso della famiglia, e ci entra con 15.000 Pa di aspirazione e l a stessa navigazione laser dei modelli superiori . Per lavare usa un panno in microfibra lavabile fino a 30 volte e il sistema SmartScrub, che strofina con più decisione e pulisce due volte più a fondo .

L'acqua, o il detergente, si dosa su tre livelli . Con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, memorizza fino a tre mappe per le case su più piani e supera soglie e dislivelli fino a 19 mm .

Chi non vuole nemmeno svuotare il contenitore può sceglierlo con la base AutoEmpty . A fine ciclo il robot ci rientra e la base aspira lo sporco in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri , che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e si sigilla quando lo si estrae, così la polvere non torna nell'aria. Un sacchetto dura fino a tre mesi: in pratica si cambia quattro volte l'anno .

Con il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash cambia il modo di lavare, perché al posto del panno singolo arrivano i DualClean, due panni rotanti che girano a 200 giri al minuto e, insieme a SmartScrub, premono sul pavimento per staccare le macchie secche. L'aspirazione sale a 20.000 Pa, e Carpet Boost la aumenta da sola quando il robot passa su un tappeto . In ogni caso, s ui tappeti i panni si sollevano di 10 mm e in modo da lasciare asciutto ciò che non deve essere lavato.

La vera novità è la base AutoWash . Oltre a svuotare il robot nel sacchetto AllergenLock già visto sul 115, lava i panni dopo ogni ciclo e li asciuga con aria calda a 45 °C , così non restano umidi e non fanno cattivo odore.

Ha due serbatoi separati, uno per l'acqua pulita e uno per quella sporca , e un ciclo di autopulizia che risciacqua la base. Il robot torna a lavare con panni puliti e il proprietario se ne occupa una volta ogni tre mesi circa.

Il Roomba 515 Combo + AutoWash porta l'acqua calda nella base AutoWash: dopo ogni ciclo i panni DualClean vengono lavati con acqua calda e poi asciugati a 60 °C . L'aspirazione arriva a 22.000 Pa.

Per parlare del suo secondo punto di forza bisogna "seguire i bordi". Con PerfectEdge la spazzola laterale si allunga e i panni si estendono verso l'esterno , fino dentro gli angoli e lungo i battiscopa, con il 18% di superficie coperta in più. Anche la batteria fa un salto in avanti: fino a 295 minuti di autonomia, abbastanza per circa 185 metri quadrati con una carica. Per gli appartamenti su più livelli le mappe memorizzabili passano da 3 a 5 , e Spot Clean manda il robot su una macchia precisa senza dover rifare tutta la stanza.

Al vertice della famiglia c'è il robot più attento. Il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash usa ClearView Pro LiDAR, che costruisce mappe in 3D e rileva gli ostacoli ad altezze diverse, e lo affianca a PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera con riconoscimento delle immagini.

Cavi, calzini e i bisogni dell'animale di casa vengono riconosciuti e aggirati , e non serve più riordinare il pavimento prima di far partire la pulizia. La stessa visione distingue lo sporco secco da quello bagnato e fa ripassare il robot dove serve.

Nella base AutoWash i panni vengono lavati con acqua fino a 75 °C, e poi asciugati con aria calda . L'aspirazione tocca i 25.000 Pa, il valore più alto dei quattro, i panni si estendono di 35 mm verso i bordi e il robot supera soglie fino a 35 mm , quindi passa senza fatica anche soglie particolarmente alte. Tutto questo in un corpo più piccolo del 46%, in volume, rispetto al Roomba Plus 505 Combo.

Per tutto ottobre i quattro robot sono in offerta anche su irobot.it, con spedizione gratuita e due anni di garanzia.

items.title: Roborock Saros 20, tre robot e un solo obiettivo: fare quasi tutto da soli
items.summary: Saros 20, Saros 20 Neo e Saros 20 Flow Complete condividono 36.000 Pa di aspirazione e tanta automazione, ma affrontano in modo diverso tappeti, ostacoli e lavaggio dei pavimenti ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Un robot aspirapolvere di fascia alta non si misura più soltanto dalla potenza con cui raccoglie polvere e detriti. La vera differenza, semmai, sta nella capacità di muoversi senza assistenza, adattarsi alle superfici, riconoscere gli ostacoli, lavare efficacemente e occuparsi autonomamente di buona parte della propria manutenzione. In breve: fare quasi tutto da soli.

È da queste basi che Roborock ha disegnato e progettato la famiglia Saros 20, composta da tre modelli (Saros 20, Saros 20 Neo e Saros 20 Flow Complete) che condividono alcuni elementi importanti, a cominciare dai 36.000 Pa di aspirazione HyperForce.

Ma non sono semplicemente tre gradini della stessa scala. Saros 20 è il modello che mette insieme chassis adattivo, navigazione 3D e una gestione particolarmente evoluta delle diverse superfici. Saros 20 Neo punta soprattutto sulla capacità di raggiungere zone difficili e muoversi nelle abitazioni più articolate. E Saros 20 Flow Complete invece cambia le impostazione sul lavaggio, sostituendo i tradizionali mop con un rullo SpiraFlow 2.0 continuamente alimentato con acqua pulita. Tre interpretazioni di una visione unica per evolvere la pulizia della casa.

La prima particolarità del Saros 20 è evidente già osservando il modo in cui si muove. Lo chassis AdaptiLift 3.0 combina ruote principali e ausiliarie sollevabili con un braccio dedicato al superamento degli ostacoli, permettendo al robot di modificare dinamicamente il proprio assetto. Significa, in altre parole, che può affrontare soglie a doppio livello alte complessivamente fino a 8,8 cm , suddivise tra un primo dislivello di 4,5 cm e un secondo di 4,3 cm. Il sistema può intervenire anche sull'inclinazione del corpo macchina per cercare di liberare il robot quando rimane intrappolato in una situazione particolarmente complicata.

Oltre che al superamento degli ostacoli, questa possibilità aiuta durante le operazioni di pulizia. Per esempio, sui tappeti lo chassis può rialzarsi per mantenere un migliore contatto della spazzola con le fibre, anche su superfici con pelo fino a 3 cm quando la relativa funzione viene abilitata dall’app.

Inoltre Saros 20 è alto appena 7,95 cm. Una misura resa possibile anche dalla scelta di utilizzare il sistema di navigazione StarSight 2.0 al posto di una tradizionale torre LiDAR sporgente. StarSight 2.0 costruisce una rappresentazione tridimensionale dell'ambiente e raggiunge una frequenza di campionamento 21 volte superiore rispetto alla propria tecnologia LDS tradizionale.

Il riconoscimento comprende oltre 300 tipologie di oggetti comuni, mentre VertiBeam lavora lateralmente per aiutare il robot a seguire pareti e mobili e a gestire elementi come i cavi.

A rendere davvero speciale Saros 20 è il modo in cui chassis, spazzola principale e doppi mop rotanti possono modificare contemporaneamente la propria posizione in funzione della superficie.

Su un tappeto, per esempio, il robot può sollevare telaio e mop e contemporaneamente abbassare e stabilizzare la spazzola principale per aumentare il contatto con le fibre. Se si sceglie la sola aspirazione, i mop possono essere lasciati automaticamente nella stazione; durante il solo lavaggio è invece la spazzola principale a sollevarsi, così da limitare il trasferimento di polvere nella zona appena inumidita. A occuparsi delle zone più vicine alle pareti c'è FlexiArm, sistema estensibile studiato per raggiungere battiscopa, angoli e mobili.

La potenza di aspirazione HyperForce raggiunge 36.000 Pa, mentre la spazzola principale DuoDivide e quella laterale FlexiArm Arc sono progettate per ridurre l'accumulo di capelli e peli intorno alle parti rotanti.

Per il lavaggio ci sono due mop rotanti fino a 200 giri al minuto . La pressione esercitata sul pavimento può passare dagli 8 N del funzionamento ordinario fino a 13 N quando viene selezionata la modalità dedicata allo sporco più difficile. In quest'ultimo caso il robot modifica anche la distribuzione del proprio peso per aumentare il contatto dei mop con il pavimento.

Inoltre, la funzione StainTarget AI Cleaning può modificare la strategia in base al tipo di sporco rilevato . In presenza di liquidi, per esempio, Saros 20 può passare al solo lavaggio mantenendo sollevate le spazzole.

Una volta terminata la pulizia entra in gioco la RockDock. La stazione può lavare i mop utilizzando acqua fino a 100 °C e successivamente asciugarli con aria calda fino a 55 °C. La base gestisce anche il riempimento automatico dell'acqua, il dosaggio del detergente e lo svuotamento della polvere. Il risultato? Fino a 65 giorni tra una sostituzione del sacchetto e l'altra, in funzione naturalmente della frequenza e delle condizioni di utilizzo.

Saros 20 viene proposto al prezzo suggerito di 1.489 euro ed è in vendita anche su Amazon : e fino al 21 ottobre è in offerta a 949 euro.

Il Saros 20 Neo parte da alcuni degli stessi concetti, ma concentra ancora maggiormente l'attenzione sulla mobilità. Anche in questo caso è stato integrato lo chassis AdaptiLift 3.0 e la possibilità di attraversare, nelle condizioni specificate dal produttore, soglie a doppio livello fino a 8,8 cm. Ma uno degli elementi che più lo caratterizzano è il profilo di appena 7,95 cm , che gli permette di insinuarsi sotto letti, divani e mobili particolarmente bassi.

La navigazione si affida, in questo caso, a Reactive AI Obstacle Recognition, abbinato alla tecnologia laterale VertiBeam. Fotocamera RGB e luce strutturata servono a individuare gli ostacoli davanti e ai lati del robot, riducendo la necessità di liberare completamente il pavimento prima di ogni pulizia.

Anche sul Neo ritroviamo i 36.000 Pa HyperForce e il sistema Dual Anti-Tangle, con la spazzola principale DuoDivide affiancata dalla FlexiArm Arc laterale.

Il lavaggio del Saros 20 Neo utilizza mop rotanti che raggiungono i 200 giri al minuto e possono esercitare fino a 14 N di pressione verso il basso. La nuova struttura dei panni è pensata per trattenere meglio l'umidità : il sistema può lasciare fino al 30% in meno di acqua residua rispetto alla precedente generazione.

È prevista anche una modalità dedicata alla pulizia dei tappeti. Neo può staccare automaticamente i mop e lasciarli alla base prima di aspirare le superfici tessili. Lo chassis adattivo può modificare la propria altezza sui tappeti fino a 3 cm di pelo , mentre nella pulizia profonda la spazzola principale viene mantenuta in una posizione più stabile per favorire la raccolta dei detriti.

Il Saros 20 Neo può coprire fino a 350 metri quadrati con una singola carica, il che lo rende adatto alla gestione di abitazioni particolarmente ampie.

La base multifunzione del Saros 20 Neo si occupa di buona parte delle operazioni che altrimenti rimarrebbero a carico dell'utente. I mop possono essere lavati con acqua fino a 100 °C, mentre un sistema di rilevamento dello sporco può modificare la durata del ciclo e richiedere al robot di effettuare un nuovo passaggio nelle aree che ne hanno bisogno.

Terminato il lavaggio, i mop vengono asciugati con aria calda fino a 55 °C. La stazione si occupa anche del riempimento con acqua calda e del dosaggio automatico del detergente.

Saros 20 Neo viene proposto al prezzo suggerito di 1.299 euro ed è in vendita anche su Amazon , dove spesso è oggetto di offerte e promozioni.

Saros 20 Flow Complete sceglie un'impostazione differente. Il punto attorno a cui ruota (letteralmente) il progetto è SpiraFlow 2.0. Anziché utilizzare una coppia di mop, il robot adotta un rullo lavapavimenti che viene continuamente alimentato con acqua pulita durante il movimento.

Il sistema utilizza 16 ugelli per distribuire acqua pressurizzata sul rullo , che può raggiungere 240 giri al minuto ed esercitare fino a 15 N di pressione verso il basso.

Ciò serve a evitare uno dei limiti tipici dei sistemi di lavaggio più semplici: continuare a trascinare sul pavimento un elemento che ha già raccolto lo sporco nelle zone precedenti. Al contrario, SpiraFlow 2.0 continua a idratare il rullo con acqua pulita e separa quella sporca raccolta durante il lavoro.

Il sistema RGB del Flow Complete viene sfruttato anche per riconoscere il tipo di pavimento e modificare automaticamente la quantità d'acqua utilizzata. Anche Saros 20 Flow Complete riduce fino al 30% delle macchie d'acqua lasciate dal rullo ad alta densità rispetto alle generazioni precedenti.

Quando arriva su un tappeto, il rullo può sollevarsi fino a 15 mm e viene protetto per separare maggiormente la parte umida dalla superficie tessile. L'utente può anche scegliere dall'app se aumentare l'aspirazione e pulire il tappeto oppure fare in modo che il robot lo eviti . In più, il rullo può estendersi lateralmente fino a 44 mm e arrivare a circa 10 mm dalla parete, mentre la spazzola laterale si occupa degli angoli.

Per il Flow Complete, Roborock utilizza RetractSense: negli spazi aperti il modulo LiDAR rimane sollevato per effettuare la scansione a 360 gradi, mentre quando il robot deve entrare sotto un mobile può ritrarsi all'interno del corpo. In questa situazione viene utilizzata anche una visuale posteriore di 100 gradi per mantenere la navigazione negli spazi più stretti.

items.title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
items.summary: Two men tell of the work they say they have been doing to support Ukrainian intelligence during the war.
items.content:
Two Russian men secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services have given rare accounts of operations they claim to have been involved with, that have targeted military assets and personnel inside Russia.

One of the men, whom we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role from Russia in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil.

He features in a BBC World Service documentary about the shadowy world of Russian saboteurs.

The documentary, by independent Polish journalist Marcin Mamon, also features a man we are calling Foma, a Russian living in exile in Poland.

Foma runs a network of undercover volunteers in Russia, that surveils high-level officers that the GUR - Ukraine's military intelligence service - is considering targeting, he says. He stresses they are never involved in the attacks themselves.

He was also tight-lipped about who they were surveilling, but after Lt Gen Fanil Sarvarov was assassinated in December last year in Moscow , Foma admitted he had provided the Ukrainians with intelligence on him.

There have been previous media reports of Russian sabotage groups, but it is rare to get access to someone operating on the ground, like Ivan, explaining alleged activities.

The GUR has confirmed that Ivan and Foma are both working for the agency. But it also has acknowledged that it cannot know the full picture. When Ivan's handler was pressed on whether he could be trusted, the handler replied: "I'm not sure of anyone, except myself."

And both the GUR and the men are cautious about how much detail they share, making it impossible to verify the activities the men claim to have carried out.

The broad tactics Ivan and Foma describe, however, have been acknowledged by the Ukrainian authorities. Kyiv has spoken of its strategy of co-ordinated drone attacks on what it claims are legitimate targets inside Russia, and has acknowledged it uses secret agents for this.

There have also been several political assassinations in Russia since the start of the war. As a matter of policy, Ukraine never officially admits or claims responsibility for targeted attacks, though a Ukrainian intelligence officer has previously admitted to the BBC it was behind the killing of senior military figure Lt Gen Igor Kirillov in December 2024.

It is difficult to confirm how many Russians are doing this kind of work for Ukraine. According to Foma, they number about 300-500, though this is impossible to verify.

If you are outside the UK, watch on YouTube , external and listen to the BBC World Service Documentary Podcast - Shadowmen: Russians working with Ukraine

Ivan and Foma say they are both opposed not just to Russia's war in Ukraine, but to President Vladimir Putin's regime - and believe his political future depends on the war's outcome.

"At the moment... I think the [Putin] regime might fall if they lose the war… Through our actions... we are trying to speed this up," Ivan says.

His work, he told Mamon, involved surveilling military sites, and locating places to hide drone components, in preparation for potential attacks on Russian assets.

"When these [drone] components are combined… it turns out a formidable weapon, which with a single blow can destroy an object that costs many, many millions of dollars," Ivan said.

He sent Mamon a video which showed him apparently hiding explosives near a Russian military airfield.

If he had been caught, he would have been charged with terrorism, and jailed for decades.

Foma's work is different - he operates remotely, training his volunteers in Russia, online. Mamon watched him conducting one such tutorial - on how to trail a senior military official marked for surveillance.

"You will get a file... from me or a colleague… with the proposed target. The file will contain [the target's] photo, his data, his details, date of birth, age, and a description of him. There'll be information on his car, if he has one. When you go to the target, don't take a phone," he told his volunteers.

Foma was once part of the Russian elite, so he claims to have a unique set of contacts and constant flow of insider information.

He showed Mamon on his laptop how he mapped military targets.

"This shows a database... the location of storage warehouses, and military units. Where generals live… Where the pilots of strategic bombers who shell Ukraine live.

"In order to break the system, you need to understand how it works. Then you can aim for their weak points."

He said there were about "three dozen" people in his network split between Russia, Ukraine and elsewhere in Europe, with the contingent outside Russia providing logistical support, such as tracking targets' digital footprints.

Foma stressed that the GUR suggests the targets to be surveilled, but that he and his team check for themselves that these individuals should be considered military criminals.

"As a rule… we also check the data [on that person]… Only after that we say whether we work or not."

"I want people who do terrible things on behalf of Putin and Russia in Ukraine… to understand that they'll have to pay for it. I want them to get scared."

Foma stressed that he only passed on intelligence to the Ukrainians, and his network did not carry out any assassinations themselves.

Of the assassination of Gen Sarvarov, killed in December 2025, he later texted Mamon to say: "Keeping track of him took quite an effort. He lived alternately with his mistress and his colleague. Covered his tracks and constantly changed his schedule."

But Foma did not share any plans with Mamon and the BBC in advance.

Ivan, however, was tight-lipped about the work he had been involved with, even after the event.

After checking with his military intelligence contacts in both Ukraine and Russia, he thought it likely that Ivan had been involved in a plan to strike Russia's largest military drone factory at Yelabuga in June last year , external . One person was reported to have been killed in the incident.

Ivan stressed that the aim is always to try to avoid harming civilians.

"The most serious case was when my car was stopped for inspection and I had the handmade explosives on me. The risk was very high - however as you can see, I was not detected," he said.

To mitigate the risk of being compromised, "there is no clear structure" to the work, he said, adding he had never met and did not know the identity of others he had been working alongside.

"As soon as you start gathering people in groups, in general chats… leaving a mark on the internet, with a high probability this whole group will be quickly detained or destroyed," he said.

Ivan stressed there were few people left in Russia suitable for this kind of work.

"Most of the ideological people have either left the country or are already behind bars," he said.

Many Russians involved in sabotage work on their native soil are therefore either oblivious - for example lorry drivers unaware that their cargoes have been compromised - or are individuals who have been paid, the BBC understands.

Ivan, on the other hand, says he is doing this work for ideological reasons - he used to be a member of the political opposition. As such, his movements would be expected to be monitored closely by the Russian authorities.

So it was a surprise that he managed to frequently leave Russia and return.

Mamon persuaded Ivan to drive him into the Georgian desert, where they could speak freely - and asked him how the Ukrainians could trust him.

"You go to a third country… where [Ukraine's] agents meet you… and conduct lie detector tests," Ivan told him.

Mamon asked Ivan to put him in touch with one of his GUR handlers in Ukraine. This man immediately rang Ivan on speaker phone - apparently demonstrating that Ivan worked for him. They spoke in code, referring to "repairs at the school".

But later, the handler admitted he could not rule out the possibility Ivan might work for the Russians too, either voluntarily or under duress.

Foma thinks the fact that Ivan can travel freely does not necessarily constitute a red flag.

"There are all sorts of holes in [the country's governance], and if you know them, or are just lucky, then you can jump through the holes… and live in the system. Like a mouse in a piece of cheese," he told Mamon.

Perhaps more compellingly, if Ivan had also been spying for FSB, it would seem likely that he would share what he knew of Ukraine's attack plans with the Russian agency. More than a year before a devastating strike by more than 100 Ukrainian drones, Ivan had been telling Marcin there would be a major attack on strategic bombers on military airfields across Russia, though he never said when or where.

"Fear is always present," he said. "It follows me everywhere. Even if you don't do anything, you're still afraid. This is Russia."

But he was optimistic that eventually his life would change.

items.title: William Gibson and the trademarking of cyberspace
items.summary: Article URL: https://colo.to/cyberspace.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50146625 Points: 192 # Comments: 74
items.content:
From the first days of the web, people have repeated the story that Autodesk trademarked "cyberspace" and Gibson retaliated by trademarking "Eric Gullichsen".

In 1989, I was working at the Autodesk Research Lab on early virtual reality, a project started after we visited Scott Fisher at NASA Ames. Our nascent system was a 386 with a pair of Matrox graphics cards on the ISA bus, a VPL EyePhone, a Polhemus tracker, and a data glove. It ran at six to ten frames per second on models with a few hundred polygons. Sluggish, but marginally enough to get us Through the Looking Glass .

I was also spending a lot of time hanging out with Timothy Leary, whose suggestion was responsible for my quitting my job at MCC and moving to California. I'd met him at the Hackers 2.0 conference in 1986 and gave him a ride to the San Jose airport. We became fast friends, and I did quite a lot of writing with him, most of which remains unpublished. But that's a story for later. Timothy, who appears in a samizdat Autodesk virtual reality video , nicknamed our VR lab "Cyberia".

Timothy was a tremendous fan of Gibson, and considered his seminal 1984 novel Neuromancer extremely prescient about the impending digital revolution.

As our VR developments crept slowly towards becoming a product, we at Autodesk applied to register a trademark "cyberspace". Timothy informed me Gibson was plenty miffed about this, so I wrote him what I felt was a conciliatory letter, 1 though ending snarkily by quoting his own words, "The street finds its own use for things."

In reply, Gibson had his lawyers send Autodesk a letter 2 . Which I recall we ignored.

Timothy - ever the incorrigible prankster - circulated the rumor that Gibson was attempting to trademark "Eric Gullichsen" in retaliation. Then Barlow, for reasons of his own, embellished that rumor . Later amplified by Rudy Rucker .

About a year later - after I'd already left Autodesk for my VR startup, Sense8 Corporation - we were invited to the inaugural Art Futura 1990 in Barcelona. And there, in the lobby of some swank hotel, I met Gibson. He opined in a laconic drawl that although the street finds its own use for things "Autodesk is not the street" .

There was plenty of cava consumed in the small hours before the time Barcelonans sit down to eat endless rounds of tapas. As I recall, after all the many Art Futura parties we'd put the matter behind us, or close enough.

And there was a memorable visit to Gaudi's Park Güell, whose giant lizard of crazy-quilt ceramic appears in Count Zero .

So: Autodesk did apply to register Cyberspace, and Gibson really did object. But Gibson trying to trademark Eric Gullichsen was Timothy Leary's prank, propagated until it became accepted history.

items.title: How Quickly Can the DoD Rebuild and Recast the Munitions Industrial Base?
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.csis.org/analysis/how-quickly-can-dod-rebuild-and-recast-munitions-industrial-base Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50146624 Points: 69 # Comments: 82
items.content:
Recent analyses have identified the causes and consequences of shrinking munitions stockpiles . Policymakers and industry should now turn their efforts to not only rebuilding the munitions industrial base but also recasting it for the demands of modern high-intensity wars of precision and attrition. Doing so calls for both increasing the size and changing the composition of the U.S. munitions arsenal, embracing magazine breadth as well as magazine depth through equipping the joint force with a “ high-low mix ” of exquisite and affordable missiles and interceptors. The emergence of multiyear “ framework agreements ” between the Department of Defense (DOD) and contractors is important, but they need to be followed by appropriations from Congress, increased capital expenditures (CapEx) by industry, and contracts between the Pentagon and companies.

What is a realistic timeline for this rebuilding and recasting of the munitions industrial base? Looking at the president’s fiscal year 2027 budget request, subsequent initiatives, quarterly company reporting, and recent contract announcements provides a clearer picture of the planned future as well as the obstacles that need to be overcome to achieve those objectives.

Based upon the DOD’s FY 2027 budget requests and subsequent policy announcements, the Pentagon plans to significantly grow stocks of the nation’s proven and capable missiles and interceptors. For example, requests for Patriot PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhanced (MSE) interceptors have grown 839 percent, from 341 in FY 2026 (by the U.S. Army and Navy ) to 3,203 in FY 2027 (by the Army and Navy ); asks for Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptors have climbed 2,216 percent, from 37 in FY 2026 (by the Missile Defense Agency ) to 857 in FY 2027 (by the Army ); and requests for Tomahawk missiles have surged 1,740 percent, from 57 in FY 2026 (by the Navy ) to 1,049 in FY 2027 (by the Navy and Army ). While expensive, these exquisite munitions are intricately designed, high-performance systems optimized to undertake the most difficult missions. Multiyear agreements, combined with coproduction efforts under consideration as well as direct-to-supplier agreements, could potentially help to reduce the 25-to-51-month manufacturing lead time for these systems. But unfortunately, these and other exquisite legacy systems were fundamentally built for performance and not designed or funded for production at scale.

Those limitations, plus the need for a broader portfolio of munitions to better address threats such as swarms of Russian and Iranian Shahed unmanned autonomous systems, have helped lead to an increased focus on lower-cost and more producible systems. Low-cost, expendable munitions have long been included in the United States’ stockpiles, ranging from the Joint Direct Attack Munition guidance kit developed in the 1990s to the Coyote counter-unmanned aircraft system pioneered the following decade . Yet the amount of attention and capital devoted to expanding affordable options within the U.S. arsenal is dramatically growing. The Pentagon launched the Drone Dominance Program in December 2025, for example, a $1.1 billion initiative to scale domestic small drone production, remove acquisition barriers, and rapidly field some 340,000 units by the end of 2027.

Since May 2026, the Pentagon and munitions manufacturers have signed several multi-year framework agreements to rapidly field substantial inventories of low-cost cruise missiles. These efforts include the Air Force’s Family of Affordable Mass Missile ( FAMM ) program for over 27,000 air-launched cruise missiles requested over the next five years and the Low-Cost Containerized Missiles ( LCCM ) program for some 10,000 ground-launched cruise missiles delivered by the beginning of 2030. Through the Multi-Mission Affordable Capacity Effector program, the Navy plans to request roughly 4,500 hypersonic air-launched cruise missiles through FY 2031. The Army seeks to equip its air and missile defense systems with modular interceptors costing under $1,000,000 per unit under its low-cost interceptor ( LCI ) initiative. The Missile Defense Agency , meanwhile, aims to counter ballistic and hypersonic threats at less than $750,000 per interceptor through an effort of the same name. To accelerate acquisition and production timelines for these new capabilities, the DOD is holding competitions for contracts between emerging defense companies in programs such as Drone Dominance and the Army LCI and signing framework production agreements with newer firms such as Anduril , CoAspire , and Zone 5 Technologies for LCCM and FAMM. These new munitions will be welcome additions to the DOD portfolio, but government and industry need to work closely to develop, rigorously test, deliver, and effectively incorporate these low-cost systems into the joint force.

The Pentagon’s FY 2027 budget request and subsequent initiatives reinforce the shifting DOD priorities within its munitions portfolio toward more affordable weapons. As Figure 1 shows, roughly 49 percent of munitions units the DOD requested for FY 2027 cost less than $600,000 per unit, which increases to over 70 percent in FY 2031 based upon projected munitions budget requests.

As the Pentagon presses industry to rebuild weapons inventories drawn down by the ongoing conflict against Iran, DOD budget documents confirm that low-cost systems will arrive at scale before most exquisite systems, as illustrated in Figure 2. Across framework agreements with Lockheed Martin of up to seven years, the DOD anticipates growing the production capacity of PAC-3 MSE interceptors by 233 percent, from roughly 600 to 2,000 interceptors per year by 2030 ; THAAD interceptor output capacity by 317 percent, from 96 to 400 units annually; and annual Precision Strike Missile production capacity fourfold to roughly 550 missiles. Backed by a DOD procurement commitment of up to seven years, RTX also plans to raise annual production of the Tomahawk missile to more than 1,000, the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile to over 1,900, and the Standard Missile 6 (SM-6) to over 500.

Compared to the multiyear lead times that these exquisite munitions producers need to ramp production capacity, however, agreements for low-cost munitions such as LCCM and FAMM are designed to move more at the speed of commercial industry and deliver rapid and repeatable production volume. For LCCM, for example, the gap between the framework agreement’s signature in May 2026 to the expected delivery of the first 1,000 units of Anduril’s surface-launched Barracuda-500M systems in 2027 is much less than the 34 months between contract award and first delivery of Tomahawk missiles projected in the FY 2027 budget documents. FAMM is on a similarly accelerated timeline, with 1,000 units requested in 2027 and more than 5,000 units requested for delivery in 2028.

Because of the immense number of the units planned for delivery in 2026 and 2027, Drone Dominance numbers are not included in Figure 2. While the drones are obviously much smaller and have different capabilities than legacy or low-cost missiles, they show the changing nature of munitions becoming available to the joint force. Although not a part of Drone Dominance, the Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS), for example, is a reverse-engineered Iranian Shahed-136 one-way attack drone that the United States deployed in combat for the first time in Operation Epic Fury . Though complete assessments of LUCAS’s initial performance remain undisclosed, the system’s $55,000 cost per unit, 18-month concept-to-development timeline, and 500-mile range position the system as a credible low-cost complement to legacy strike systems. In his testimony before the Senate Armed Services Committee in May 2026, Admiral Brad Cooper credited LUCAS with having “ flipped the cost curve ” against Iran by making Tehran use its own higher-end weapons. U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll also informed the U.S. House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee in April 2026 that the service purchased 13,000 Merops interceptor drones—designed by United States-owned Perennial Autonomy, battle-tested in Ukraine , and costing less than $10,000 per unit—to counter Shahed drones in Iran. The Army is explicitly running a “ compressed ” timeline for its LCI program, meanwhile, placing the initial Request for Information in May 2026 and targeting the first live-fire demonstrations for fall of 2026 . It is also splitting the interceptor into subsegments and acquiring their intellectual property rights to accelerate acquisition and reduce the risk of bottlenecked production in the future.

As Figure 3 illustrates, the pace of replenishment and agreements translating into deliveries varies sharply across the munitions industrial base.

While these framework agreements and announcements suggest the munitions industrial base will significantly evolve in a short time frame, there remain large obstacles to converting plans into production. Framework agreements are not appropriations; rather, they deliver demand signals intended to instill industry with confidence in future government purchases to justify large CapEx investments in facilities, workforces, and supply chains. Whether signals translate into additional industrial capacity depends on Congress appropriating funds, the Pentagon signing contracts, and industry delivering effective systems.

items.title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
items.summary: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.
items.content:
The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies has called on the European Union to drop import restrictions on products made from the country, arguing it has been "bundled together" in measures aimed a curbing cheap imports from the likes of China.

Yuriy Ryzhenkov, chief executive of Metinvest, told the BBC the recently-imposed tariffs on imported steel to the EU were "unfair" and had been put in place "without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in".

He said he wished to see "at least a carve out" for Ukraine to access the EU market.

A spokesperson for the European Commission said the EU "took into account the difficult situation" of Ukraine when deciding its steel policy.

The trading bloc has recently imposed restrictions on steel imports in an effort to protect steel manufacturers of member nations.

It has capped the amount of steel which can enter the EU tax free at 18.3 million tonnes per year - a 47% reduction from 2024 levels.

There are some country-specific quotas in the policy, but the overall aim is to cut the amount of steel that can be imported due to member nations struggling to compete with cheap imports from the likes of China and Turkey.

Despite a free-trade agreement (FTA) being in place between the EU and Ukraine, the FTA does not stop the EU from introducing separate trade protection measures.

"Ukraine has been bundled together into those measures without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in," Ryzhenkov said, pointing to the war with Russia.

"Access to the European market is crucial for survival," he added. "The restrictive measures that have been put in place by the authorities in the European Union, they don't help.

"I think it's unfair that Ukraine has been treated in the same way as all of the other importers into the European Union."

The Ukraine steel industry estimates steel exports to the EU could ultimately fall by about 50–60%.

The EU said Ukraine's specific steel quota guaranteed exports of the metal, but acknowledged this was at a "level lower than in the past years".

"Despite the war effort, Ukraine remains an important exporter of steel to the EU," a spokesperson said, adding it had "offered compensations" to its largest suppliers, which included Ukraine.

Steel products are a foundation in Ukraine's economy. Before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, metallurgy and mining accounted for roughly 10% of Ukraine's national income and a third of its exports. The EU is its top customer.

But the industry has suffered from the continued Russian bombardment.

All of Ukraine's steel mills have been bombed at points since the conflict began in 2022, but Ryzhenkov said strikes had "intensified significantly recently".

At one point in September, there was "no single tonne of steel produced" in Ukraine for the first time in about 150 years, he added.

Almost 800 Metinvest workers have been killed since the war began.

Ryzhenkov said the company had "improved the covered areas" at its mills where workers can shelter during air raids.

"The only thing we can do is to design procedures to keep people safe and just obey those procedures and try to minimise the risks."

"Unfortunately, you cannot cover a whole steel mill to avoid it being damaged."

Ryzhenkov said he expected the coming winter to be "one of the hardest in our history".

"We are in a dire situation when we don't have logistics to access any other market apart from the EU and cutting our available market by 60%, that doesn't help for the industry to survive."

items.title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
items.summary: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.
items.content:
US President Donald Trump has said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table.

"I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine," Trump said on his Truth Social messaging platform, adding that he didn't want to "do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table".

Trump blocked numerous sanctions on Russia on Friday night, two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky deepened.

Zelensky told NBC News on Sunday that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a "historic mistake".

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev has responded to Trump's order by calling it "an important and truly historic moment". He said the sanctions, which were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September, would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has described the suspension of the sanctions as a 60-day pause during which their potential impact on the US and global economies would be analysed.

In his Truth Social post, Trump also said Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did", adding "he could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now".

Zelensky has pushed for an end to fighting, and has repeatedly said that Putin doesn't want peace, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week.

Despite the international sanctions, Russia has still been able to export oil, much of it to China and India - often at attractive discounts. According to the think-tank Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), China has taken about half of Russia's crude exports, with India accounting for about 37%.

In remarks to a European Union summit, after Trump announced the deal to buy diesel from Russia and said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Putin, Zelensky said it was nice to be among "real leaders".

Zelensky has repeatedly pushed for stringent sanctions to limit funding that Russia can use in its war effort. After the latest move from the US, however, he said he believed the Trump administration would lift more sanctions against Russia.

Ukraine and its European allies criticised Trump's plans to import Russian diesel to help lower US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war.

The deal, according to Zelensky, was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Concerns that Trump is siding with Russia have been heightened by disruption to Starlink, a US-provided satellite system used by Ukraine. That hampered Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks.

Zelensky said US officials had linked speed restrictions to technical issues.

However, he said Ukraine had tested Starlink on EU territory and found it was operating at higher speeds.

Trump has denied both deliberately slowing down the network and a further accusation from Zelensky that the US had stopped sharing defence intelligence.

items.title: Show HN: WhatsApp MCP running free on Cloudflare
items.summary: I wanted my humble Claude on mobile to access my WhatsApp messages but the only options I could find either required WhatsApp Business or an actual server to run Baileys on. I wanted to run it for free on ClaudeFlare and with my personal WhatsApp account, so I built this. Important feature - it connects to your Google account as well as WhatsApp to grab the names of all your WhatsApp contacts, otherwise you get only phone numbers for many of them and search doesn't work properly. This is a single user install because it's both gray area and very private - so point your agent at the repo and le
items.content:
This is a small server that runs in your own Cloudflare account. You link your phone to it once, the way you'd link WhatsApp Web, and from then on any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, anything that speaks MCP) can search and read your chats. It can read and search your messages, and remember names you give it for phone numbers. It can't send anything.

Your phone stays the source of truth. The server is a linked device that your agent talks to.

It doesn't stay connected to WhatsApp. When your agent asks for something, and once a day, it connects, collects whatever WhatsApp queued for it since last time, writes that to its own database, and hangs up. Your phone keeps working normally and keeps getting notifications.

Your messages live in a SQLite database inside a Durable Object in your Cloudflare account. Nothing goes anywhere else.

You need a Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan (see the note below), Node 20 or later, and your phone.

Wrangler prints your URL, something like https://whatsapp-mcp.your-name.workers.dev . Open it. The front page has the two remaining steps:

Link WhatsApp. Scan the QR code with WhatsApp (Settings, Linked Devices, Link a Device). If you're on the phone itself and can't scan a screen, use the phone number option instead. The first link imports your history. The page shows progress, and you can close it.

Then type /mcp and sign in with the password. Other clients: point them at the same /mcp URL.

If you want your own domain, see the comments at the bottom of wrangler.jsonc .

Importing a large history decodes a lot of data in one go, and the default CPU limit on Workers is too small for it. wrangler.jsonc raises it, and raising it needs the paid plan, which is a few dollars a month. I haven't tried the free plan. If you're on it, remove the limits block and expect the first import to be fragile.

This isn't official. WhatsApp has no API for reading your own personal messages. This uses the same protocol WhatsApp Web uses, through an open source library (Baileys). That's against WhatsApp's terms. For a linked device that only reads, the practical risk is low, but it isn't zero. Use it on your own account, and don't use it to send messages.

You get what WhatsApp sends. The first link imports whatever history WhatsApp decides to hand a new device. It may not be everything. It only does this once per link. To import again, relink (your stored messages are kept, and a re-import fills in anything missing).

Some chats show up as phone numbers. WhatsApp doesn't give a linked device every contact name, and most of these are one-off messages from people you never saved. For the ones that matter, your agent can fix it: it lists the unnamed chats, looks the numbers up in your contacts with whatever contacts tool it already has (a Google Contacts or Gmail connector, for example), and saves the names. The server never connects to a contacts service itself. See "Naming chats" below.

Media isn't downloaded. Photos, voice notes and documents appear as labels like [image] or [voice note 12s] , with the caption if there was one. Nothing is transcribed.

It's for one person. One deployment is one WhatsApp account and one owner. That's deliberate: each deployment holds a full message history and a live login to the account, so everyone should run their own.

Relinking. If your phone says the device was removed, or you want to start over, ask your agent to run relink , or open /setup and choose "Unlink and scan again". You scan a new QR code. Stored messages are kept.

Every read tool first tops up from WhatsApp if the stored copy is more than ten minutes old.

WhatsApp only gives this server the names it knows. The rest show up as phone numbers. Rather than have the server log in to a contacts service (which means a cloud project, consent screens and, for Google, an app review), it hands the job to your agent, which usually already has a way to reach your contacts.

Say "find names for my unnamed chats". The agent calls unnamed_chats , matches the numbers against your contacts, and saves what it finds with set_contact_names . It won't find everyone: most unnamed chats are a single message from a stranger.

Agents get nudged toward this on their own. The server's instructions mention it, and so does every "no chat found" and "no matches" result, because that's the moment an agent is stuck on a name. link_status also says how many chats are unnamed.

Everything below is for whoever is changing the code, including an AI agent working on a fork. The top of this file is for the person who owns the deployment.

One Durable Object holds everything. Its SQLite is both the Baileys auth store and the message store. The Worker is stateless apart from a KV namespace the OAuth provider uses for tokens and a short-lived "pending sign-in" record.

All WhatsApp traffic happens inside runSession() in whatsapp-do.ts . There are two kinds:

Callers share one session: a second pull() while one is running gets the same promise.

A pairing session outlives the HTTP request that started it. startPairing sets a Durable Object alarm, and alarm() awaits the session promise. An in-flight alarm handler is what keeps the object alive. The pairing page only watches; closing it doesn't stop the import.

Idle detection counts only data events ( messaging-history.set , messages.upsert ), not connection chatter. Counting everything keeps a session open forever, because presence and contact updates never stop.

All in the Durable Object's SQLite ( store.ts , initSchema ).

Ingest is idempotent. Re-importing history upserts: it fills in a missing sender or push_name and never duplicates. That is what makes relinking safe.

These all cost real time to find. Read them before touching the Baileys parts.

Keep a deployment's own values (domain, KV id, email) in wrangler.local.jsonc , which is gitignored, and deploy with npm run deploy:local . wrangler.jsonc is the template other people start from.

With PIN set, these return JSON and need the header x-pin: :

Local development: npm run dev with a .dev.vars containing OWNER_PASSWORD=... (12+ characters). It runs a local Durable Object with its own empty storage, so you can exercise the sign-in flow and see a real QR code, but linking a phone from local dev makes a second linked device.

To test the pairing UI states without a phone, serve the page with a mocked /pair/status . Everything the page needs is that one JSON shape: paired , running , progress , qrSvg , messages , chats .

items.title: Trump sostiene Netanyahu nelle prossime elezioni israeliane, nonostante la guerra in Iran
items.content:
Domenica il presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump ha ufficialmente preso posizione in vista delle elezioni in Israele del 27 ottobre, dicendo di sostenere il primo ministro uscente Benjamin Netanyahu. Trump finora non si era pronunciato e il sostegno non era scontato, visto che gli ottimi rapporti fra i due leader di destra si erano guastati dopo la guerra in Iran. Lo scorso febbraio Netanyahu aveva di fatto convinto Trump ad attaccare il regime iraniano, prospettandogli una facile vittoria che non si è realizzata: la guerra ha invece provocato una crisi energetica globale e sta danneggiando Trump e il Partito Repubblicano in vista delle elezioni di metà mandato a novembre.

I due si erano poi nuovamente incontrati a luglio, durante una visita di Netanyahu alla Casa Bianca, in cui il primo ministro israeliano aveva cercato di ricucire i rapporti. Domenica sera Trump ha scritto un post sul suo social Truth in cui definisce Netanyahu un «grande primo ministro guerriero e un ancora più grande partner per la pace». Trump ha quindi invitato gli israeliani a votare lui e il suo partito, il Likud, nelle elezioni che definiranno la composizione del nuovo parlamento, le prime dopo gli attacchi di Hamas del 7 ottobre 2023 e la guerra a Gaza.

I sondaggi indicano le coalizioni guidate da Netanyahu e dal generale Gadi Eisenkot praticamente alla pari. Netanyahu ha subito ringraziato Trump per l’endorsement: il presidente statunitense è molto popolare in Israele, anche se non è mai possibile dire quanto queste dichiarazioni di sostegno possano davvero influenzare il voto.

I think the title captures the idea fully but I'll dig into it because this ain't Twitter. You're working an idea, a piece of code, or a multibillion a year SaaS app which is probably saving the world. Maybe you're automating the cloning process of grabbing new Labubu release images and taking the 2D image and using a ComfyUI to translate it into a 3D CAD to get the replica production started faster because CNY is on the horizon and global manufacturing halts around that time. Maybe you like to use your tokens to search against the most powerful computer software ever developed for macronutrient information for a McRib or some shit. You're most likely chatting with some type of frontend thats tied into a paid subscription from the provider of your choice. TUI, GUI, Voice call, whatever. It's your data going in and their data coming back for you. That's what they're selling, I'm happy to buy that right now. They'll show you something like this as proof of work happening:

That is a distraction. That is not token usage statistics with time series data meant for engineers. I can't make a decision with this bullshit. Surely the big labs will have valuable insight to share with the curious user who digs into the Analytics panel.

I can't make a decision with this bullshit. I hear you already, "there's OTel export options!!1!". Cool, I guess. This is one reason, here's 5 more off of the top of my head right now:

I'm not going to suggest a proxy provider for you to use, only that you run it yourself somewhere you control. When you pick one, don't forget you can modify it for your actual needs. I've modded mine for better insight, for custom MCP server endpoints, additional features. Whatever you choose, you should be getting something along these lines for data.

When I see a cache miss during a coding session, I can pinpoint why that happened in 20 seconds by hand. I haven't automated it but the proxy I use has an API, so it's possible to automate. Own your infrastructure, your application visibility, data pathing, and storage. I do this at home because it's fun and it's how I like to learn. I do this at work because I'm not doing my job right if I don't. I may never fully understand how the fuck a large language model works well enough to white board it in an interview. But I can wrassle it down and make sure it's instrumented while serving inference.

Warning: This video contains descriptions of drug-taking and distressing images

A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump pledged a crackdown on drug cartels, proscribing many as terrorist organisations.

Drug overdose deaths have fallen from a peak of around 110,000 in 2022, down to roughly 70,000 last year.

However, America's decades-long drug crisis may be accelerating and authorities are increasingly concerned about cheaper, more powerful synthetic drugs, including an animal tranquilliser called tranq.

items.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
items.summary: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.
items.content:
Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him. "We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."

The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California. Police said officials are investigating his death as a suspected overdose.

Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

Crawford wrote in the post on Sunday: "We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years."

"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," she also posted.

"Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia," she wrote in closing, with an emoji of angel wings.

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner lists Gerber's case as pending additional investigation. The Santa Monica Police Department has said there is no indication foul play was involved in his death.

Gerber's sister Kaia also dedicated a post to him on Sunday which included a video of the two siblings as children dancing together, a photo of them standing near the ocean, and a four-page letter to "prez" typed out on a blue background.

In the letter, she said she had been scared of getting her ears pierced, so "you went first".

"But when I held the earring they took from your body, all I could think was: That belongs to you," she wrote.

"I am learning how to love you when I cannot see you," she also wrote. "How to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you. How to be your sister in a world that I can't reach for you in," she wrote.

In recent years, Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use and frequently posted videos on Instagram himself for what he called "Mental Health Mondays".

His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.

If you're affected by any of the issues in this article you can find details of organisations who can help via the BBC Action Line.

Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide , external , external.

items.title: Emmanuel Macron ha detto che in Francia potrebbero essere vietate «alcune manifestazioni» per proteggere le città dalla violenza
items.content:
Il presidente francese Emmanuel Macron ha tenuto un discorso alla nazione il giorno dopo le proteste in decine di città francesi. Macron ha detto che la Francia prova «rabbia e vergogna» per quanto accaduto ai margini delle proteste e che nei prossimi giorni i prefetti prenderanno tutte le «decisioni necessarie per proteggere le città», che potrebbero arrivare anche a «proibire alcune manifestazioni». Sabato centinaia di migliaia di persone hanno partecipato a manifestazioni pacifiche, ma ci sono stati anche molti scontri tra polizia e manifestanti , atti di vandalismo contro edifici, saccheggi, e numerosi incendi.

Macron ha detto che le violenze sono state causate da «rivoltosi provenienti da gruppuscoli di estrema sinistra, ai quali si sono uniti numerosi delinquenti» e ha invitato le istituzioni giudiziarie a perseguirli. Ha annunciato iniziative per venire incontro al carovita e all’aumento del prezzo dei carburanti, nonché per ascoltare le richieste degli studenti riguardo alla scuola. Ha poi invitato tutte le forze politiche a collaborare per ritrovare un clima di calma anche in vista delle prossime elezioni presidenziali.

Da domenica pomeriggio però a Parigi ci sono stati nuovi disordini , seppur minori rispetto a quelli di sabato: intorno a piazza de la République si sono radunate varie centinaia di persone, e alcune hanno assaltato negozi, dato fuoco a biciclette elettriche, danneggiato alcune strutture.

items.title: Da Putin a Dylan Dog, la nuova stagione a teatro in 10 titoli
items.summary: Ancora tanto Pirandello, ma anche i De Filippo e inediti
items.content: Dall'anniversario di Pirandello al ritorno di Dylan Dog, passando per biografie e indagini, a tutto tondo, dell'animo umano e le tempeste che lo attraversano. E' l'affresco dell'avvio della nuova stagione teatrale in 10 titoli al debutto, e poi in tournée, da non perdere da qui a Natale. LO ZAR - Dopo il successo in tv, Stefano Massini porta anche in palcoscenico, fino al 18 ottobre al Teatro Era di Pontedera (PI) e poi in tournée, Lo Zar, il suo potente monologo su Vladimir Putin. Una biografia tratta dal libro e dalle conferenze dello stesso leader del Cremlino, che sulle tracce della scalata irresistibile di un ex adolescente teppista (come Putin stesso si definisce) diventa riflessione sul significato del potere. OSCAR - Meglio abbandonarsi all'amore o lottare per i propri ideali? È più potente il senso di lealtà o quello di giustizia? Prosegue il sodalizio tra Antonio Latella e Sonia Bergamasco che in questa stagione diventa l'eroina cresciuta come uomo nella Francia del XVII secolo. Debutto al Piccolo di Milano il 20 ottobre. L'ULTIMO NASTRO DI KRAPP / PRESS CONFERENCE - Per l'apertura di stagione dello Stabile di Napoli, Roberto Andò prende due giganti della scrittura come Samuel Beckett e Harold Pinter e costruisce un dittico sul rapporto fra parola, memoria e potere. Protagonista, Renato Carpentieri, al debutto il 21 ottobre al Mercadante. LE ULTIME LUNE - Dopo il successo de La coscienza di Zeno, Alessandro Haber torna a farsi dirigere da Paolo Valerio nel testo scritto negli anni '90 da Furio Bordon e rappresentato per la prima volta in Italia con un indimenticabile Marcello Mastroianni nel ruolo del protagonista: un anziano che attende l'ingresso in una casa di cura (dal 27 ottobre al Carignano di Torino). DYLAN DOG HORROR SHOW - Per i 40 anni dell'indagatore dell'incubo nato dalla matita di Tiziano Sclavi, Valter Malosti firma il primo spettacolo ufficiale dedicato a Dylan Dog e la prima produzione teatrale di Sergio Bonelli Editore. In prima nazionale dal 28 ottobre con Gabriele Graham Gasco protagonista, lo spettacolo è già un evento, perché dopo sei anni segna la riapertura dell'Eliseo di Roma. NON SI SA COME - Nel pieno dei 90 anni dalla morte di Luigi Pirandello, Franco Branciaroli diretto da Paolo Valerio è il conte Romeo Daddi, uomo oppresso dal rimorso per un'azione compiuta senza motivo apparente, nell'ultimo dramma compiuto del Premio Nobel. Debutto al Rossetti di Trieste il 29 ottobre. OTELLO e PECCATO FOSSE UNA SGUALDRINA - Luca De Fusco firma due spettacoli in un ideale dittico su tre temi universali: il desiderio, la colpa e la violenza morale. Nel primo, porta Shakespeare in un immaginario sud coloniale negli anni più segnati dal razzismo del Novecento (debutto 4 novembre all'Argentina di Roma); e l'amore proibito di John Ford, invece, in una scena astratta e multimediale, tra specchi e videoproiezioni (dal 2 dicembre). Con, tra gli altri, Luca Lazzareschi, Mersila Sokoli, Federico Vanni e Gianluca Merolli. I FRATELLI DE FILIPPO - Dopo il debutto al Campania Teatro Festival, parte dal Diana di Napoli, il 18 novembre, la tournée dello spettacolo che Sergio Rubini ha tratto dal libro di Maurizio Giammusso, Vita di Eduardo (ed. Minimum Fax). In scena gli anni giovanili dei tre fratelli e quel momento d'oro, dal 1931 al 1944, quando sotto l'insegna della Compagnia del Teatro Umoristico I De Filippo, conquistarono i palcoscenici di tutta Italia. ORLANDO - Dal capolavoro di Virginia Woolf, Giuseppe Di Pasquale dirige Viola Graziosi e Arturo Cirillo in Orlando, la commedia (debutto al Verga di Catania il 24 novembre), storia del giovane e melanconico cortigiano dell'epoca di Elisabetta I, che nel corso di quasi quattro secoli si trova a vivere diverse vite e a cambiare sesso, diventando una donna. EDUCAZIONE SENTIMENTALE - Daniele Canonico, uomo medio di cinquant'anni, originario del Sud, racconta al pubblico il suo ingresso nel 'mondo dei maschi'. Dopo l'anteprima al Festival di Spoleto, Beppe Fiorello porta in tournée il nuovo atto unico di Ivan Cortoneo, a partire dal 3 dicembre al Verdi di Salerno.

items.title: In Abruzzo l'inusuale mondiale di papere galleggianti / IL VIDEO
items.summary: Una gara per l'ambiente. E, come a Berlino per calcio, vittoria dell'Italia sulla Francia
items.content: 'Il cielo è azzurro sopra Goriano', avrebbero commentato i più navigati giornalisti sportivi. Proprio come accadde a Berlino vent'anni fa, l'Italia infatti torna campione del mondo battendo di misura i cugini francesi. Non a calcio, ma nell'inusuale gara di papere. Galleggianti. È successo ieri in Abruzzo, nel Parco Sirente-Velino, a una quarantina di chilometri dall'Aquila, dove gli azzurri hanno conquistato il primo World Duck Race Championship. Stavolta senza neanche passare per la lotteria dei calci di rigore. Terza la Moldavia, a poca distanza. Dietro il podio, un sorteggio degno di un torneo iridato: 197 papere per altrettante rappresentanze, 195 Paesi - tra cui Vaticano e Palestina - più Onu e Unione europea. Per la corsa ne sono state estratte quindici, così da non riversarle tutte insieme nell'Aterno, nel momento della sfida decisiva. Altre duecento circa, di dimensioni diverse, hanno partecipato alla manifestazione tra Tione degli Abruzzi e Acciano. L'idea, a dire il vero, non è nata dal nulla. Elena, una ragazza di Goriano Valli che vive a Bolzano, ha condiviso un video di una corsa analoga. E le sfide tra papere hanno già una storia internazionale: a Merano gareggiano sul Passirio dal 2018; a Londra, nel 2008, la Great British Duck Race sul Tamigi arrivò a numeri da Guinness, con 250mila papere annunciate. Qui, più modestamente, si è scelto di farle correre per una causa. Le donazioni raccolte, infatti, sosterranno il Museo Diffuso Sirente-Velino, nato a Goriano Valli, frazione di Tione degli Abruzzi. Ideato da Fausto Di Giulio, il MuDi punta a custodire la memoria delle comunità locali e a contrastare lo spopolamento dei piccoli borghi. Si ispira al principio del 'Give Back', restituire qualcosa alla propria terra, coinvolgendo anche chi è emigrato. Sedici stazioni, ricavate da antiche botteghe, cantine, stalle e abitazioni, raccontano la cultura contadina e provano a creare nuove occasioni di visita nell'entroterra. "Abbiamo scelto una papera per parlare di qualcosa di molto serio, ma con un sorriso", spiega Di Giulio, che richiama il principio One Health: la salute delle persone è legata a quella dell'ambiente. E prima ancora di affidare le papere alla corrente, volontari e partecipanti si sono messi al lavoro lungo l'Aterno, raccogliendo dodici sacchi di plastica abbandonata nel fiume e sulle sponde. Una pulizia collettiva che ha preceduto la competizione, organizzata con un sistema di recupero e conteggio di tutte le papere per evitare di lasciare rifiuti in acqua. L'impegno prosegue anche dopo il traguardo: il regolamento invita ciascun partecipante a dedicare almeno mezz'ora, entro trenta giorni, alla raccolta di rifiuti nel territorio del parco. Perché la sensibilizzazione ambientale può passare anche attraverso delle papere di plastica.

items.title: Un drone ucraino ha sconfinato e si è schiantato in Lituania: due jet italiani erano decollati per abbatterlo
items.content:
Un drone ucraino ha sconfinato domenica mattina in Lituania, schiantandosi poi nel nord del paese, senza fare grandi danni: alcuni detriti hanno colpito un’automobile in sosta. All’arrivo del drone, allora di provenienza sconosciuta, il comando della NATO aveva risposto facendo decollare due caccia Eurofighter italiani per intercettarlo e abbatterlo. Era stato dato l’allarme nelle zone interessate dal passaggio del drone, l’aeroporto di Kaunas era stato chiuso per un’ora e i residenti erano stati invitati a mettersi al sicuro nei rifugi antiaerei.

Nel corso della giornata il ministero degli Esteri ucraino ha chiesto scusa per lo sconfinamento del drone, riconoscendo che era stato lanciato dalle forze armate ucraine, ma dicendo che era stato probabilmente deviato «da azioni di guerra elettronica da parte della Russia», che di fatto ne avevano cambiato la destinazione «durante un’operazione contro obiettivi militari legittimi in Russia».

items.title: Someone behind the software
items.summary: Article URL: https://karrisaarinen.com/posts/someone-behind-the-software/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50142573 Points: 457 # Comments: 167
items.content:
I think good products carry something of the people who make them. Their experience, what they care about, and how they think things should work. You might not know who those people are, but you can feel their perspective in the product.

The industry often talks about software as though it comes out of a factory. You collect requirements, build features, and measure whether they work. Follow the process and you should get a good result. Now we're talking automating this whole pipeline with agents.

But two teams can talk to similar customers, have access to the same technology, and make very different things. The difference comes from how they understand what they see and the style they go about building it. The founder background or company DNA also shapes this a lot.

At Linear , we have always valued intuition over process or data. I think people sometimes understand that as making decisions based on personal preference, without much thought or evidence. What we mean by it is that your intuition develops through experience and understanding. You work on something, talk to customers, make mistakes, and learn what to pay attention to. The intuition is your point of view on something, and forcing to use your judgment, not hide behind faceless data.

Before we launched, we talked to people across companies and roles about how they worked. We had our own frustrations with this type software, but those conversations helped us understand what mattered beyond our own experience. Our perspective got better after those conversations.

So eventually the products develops a character through what its makers pay attention to, what they decide not to do and what they keep working on after it technically works. I sometimes think of this as the soul of a product. You feel that someone cares about how the whole thing comes together.

A feature can work perfectly well on its own and still make the product worse. Recognizing that requires some belief about what the product should be. Someone has to make the call, then stay close enough to customers to see whether they were right.

Recently, many products are starting to feel messy to me, including products from very successful companies. There seems to be more thought going into what the technology can do and what can be added than the form it should take. The product changes are primarily additive, not improving the core problem.

I think the reasons for this is that it's lot easier to add new capabilities, than rethink existing capabilities. So each product becomes a collection of abilities, without actually having unified point of view.

I wonder whether some of this comes from how the work is organized. Individuals work with agents to produce changes independently, each operating a small software factory. Each change might make sense on its own, but together they start to resemble Frankenstein’s monster rather than a carefully shaped sculpture.

Without the shared perspective, soul, or thought, the product becomes an average of all those outputs. The choices that once gave it character are being diluted by day. More things work, but it becomes harder to feel someone or even something behind them.

Making software is getting easier. I hope that gives people more room to develop a perspective and follow it further. To understand a problem deeply and keep shaping an answer until the pieces belong together.

I want to feel the creator behind the software, not the factories.

items.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
items.summary: At least one person was killed in the strikes, which also hit a data centre used by Russia's equivalent of Facebook.
items.content:
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.

The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.

A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week.

Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing.

It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

Ukraine has struck St Petersburg before, though regions closer to Ukraine are threatened more often. The city's oil terminal was last hit in July .

Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight into Sunday.

St Petersburg's governor said 12 apartment buildings and two homes were damaged in the attacks on the city, while Pulkovo Airport was temporarily closed.

He also said mobile internet service disruption was possible.

Social network VK confirmed a drone had targeted its regional data centre, but stressed its services were available "as usual" after users reported outages in the early hours of the morning.

Ozon also confirmed its local logistics centre had been targeted by a drone, sparking a fire.

It said staff were evacuated and no one was injured, and that it was not accepting shipments from sellers at the location "as it is currently serving other operational purposes".

As well as numerous oil facilities across Russia, Ukraine has also mounted strikes aimed at disrupting the Russian economy more broadly. Earlier this month, it launched a series of attacks on Yandex, Russia's largest search engine, that led to service disruptions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have frayed since the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel in the hope of bringing down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war, ahead of the midterm elections.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Trump's decision to temporarily suspend a raft of sanctions against Russia has brought fresh criticism , including from some US Republicans.

However, on Sunday, Zelensky said on Telegram he had had conversations with Trump's top negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

He said their teams are in constant communication and preparing the next diplomatic steps.

Both Russia and Ukraine have been striking one another's energy infrastructure with increasing intensity ahead of the winter, as Moscow's full-scale invasion drags on in its fifth year.

Russia says it hits targets used by Ukraine's military, though the UN noted on Friday that the first two weeks of October had been the deadliest for Ukrainian civilians in years.

Russian strikes on energy facilities have left hundreds of thousands without power, raising concerns about civilians enduring another freezing winter.

Zelensky said on Saturday that tens of thousands of people were still without power. Russia launched nearly 2,700 drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 66 missiles in the past week, most of which were aimed at energy facilities, he said.
